independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: Ps 136 is an identity psalm (verse_map_oshb.json returns web Ps.136.V for every MT Ps.136.V; 26 verses in both witnesses), so no dual-cite arithmetic is at stake and the row's bare web:/oshb: pairing is correct. All three Hebrew splices collate at byte tier (collate.py: oshb:Ps.136.1 twice, oshb:Ps.136.3 -- byte). The opener claim re-derives exactly: psalm_device_inventory.json hodu_openings holds exactly 6 entries (Ps.33.2, Ps.105.1, Ps.107.1, Ps.118.1, Ps.118.29, Ps.136.1), all identity psalms, so the row's web: refs for the five companions resolve one-to-one; counting the object as the verse-initial FORMULA legitimately spans the two attested spellings (the defective member at 107:1), and a skeleton sweep of the plene phrase returns a different set of 6 verses (33:2, 105:1, 106:1, 118:1, 118:29, 136:1 -- 106:1 carries hodu non-initially after hallelu-Yah, 107:1 falls out on spelling), which is why the inventory and not a naive sweep is the right authority here. The refrain sweep is the row's strongest work and re-derives byte-wise: the last three words of each of Ps 136's 26 verses give 25 verses with כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ and 1 verse (136:3) with כִּ֖י לְעֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ; sweep.py --skel returns 32 VERSES book-wide for the plene tail and 1 VERSE for the defective one. The seam at 136:3|4 is sound -- 136:1, 136:2 and 136:3 all open with the imperative hodu and 136:4 opens a lamed-participle. What fails is the extent clause hung on that seam, filed below. Noted but not filed: labelling an MT orthographic variant an 'erratum-class spelling variant' imports campaign register into row prose and invites a reader to treat a witness spelling as a defect to repair.

challenges.claim: The row's claim that 136:4 replaces the imperative hodu-plus-object frame with a participial construction 'that runs through the rest of the psalm' (repeated in rejected_alternative as 'sustained through the rest of the psalm') is falsified in both witnesses: the imperative hodu-plus-object frame returns as the psalm's last verse, and the participial chain is broken by six finite-verb clauses before it.
challenges.evidence: The psalm's closing verse is ה֭וֹדוּ לְאֵ֣ל הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם (oshb:Ps.136.26), imperative plus object -- the very frame the row calls dropped -- rendered “Oh give thanks to the God of heaven,” (web:Ps.136.26). First-word inspection of verse_map_oshb.json across 136:4-25 gives lamed-participle heads in only 8 verses (136:4, 136:5, 136:6, 136:7, 136:10, 136:13, 136:16, 136:17); 6 verses open with a finite verb (136:11, 136:14, 136:15, 136:18, 136:21, 136:24), e.g. וַיּוֹצֵ֣א יִ֭שְׂרָאֵל מִתּוֹכָ֑ם (oshb:Ps.136.11) = “and brought out Israel from among them,” (web:Ps.136.11); 6 more open nominally (136:8, 136:9, 136:12, 136:19, 136:20, 136:22). The 136:3|4 seam itself is unaffected -- only the extent claim is.

reviews.reasoning: The Hebrew splice at oshb:Ps.136.5 collates byte (collate.py). I do not contest the span: 136:8-9 are accusative continuations governed by the lamed-participle of 136:7, so the creation recital coheres as one block, and the turn to Egypt at 136:10 -- which also restarts the lamed-participle head class after two nominal verses -- is a real edge. The row's other figure is correct: byte comparison of the last three words of 136:4 through 136:9 returns the plene refrain tail in all 6 verses. What fails is the form sweep, which is the row's only quantified evidence. Confidence medium is otherwise well calibrated for a content-driven internal seam.

challenges.claim: The row's central sweep -- 'Every verse (6 of 6, 136:4-9) keeps the participial "to him who..." construction' -- is false: 136:8 and 136:9 open with the object marker and contain no participle, so the figure is 4 of 6 verses, and both witnesses agree.
challenges.evidence: אֶת הַ֭שֶּׁמֶשׁ לְמֶמְשֶׁ֣לֶת בַּיּ֑וֹם (oshb:Ps.136.8) and אֶת הַיָּרֵ֣חַ וְ֭כוֹכָבִים לְמֶמְשְׁל֣וֹת בַּלָּ֑יְלָה (oshb:Ps.136.9) -- both byte tier (collate.py) -- open with the object marker and carry no participle; WEB renders them “the sun to rule by day,” (web:Ps.136.8) and “the moon and stars to rule by night,” (web:Ps.136.9), with no 'to him who' in either. The lamed-participle heads in this span number 4 verses, not 6: לְעֹ֘שֵׂ֤ה (oshb:Ps.136.4), לְעֹשֵׂ֣ה (oshb:Ps.136.5), לְרֹקַ֣ע (oshb:Ps.136.6), לְ֭עֹשֵׂה (oshb:Ps.136.7). The claim is installed three times -- rationale, observed_substrate_signals ('runs unbroken from web:Ps.136.4 through web:Ps.136.9'), and rejected_alternative ('one uninterrupted participial chain') -- so a repair is one edit across all three fields.

reviews.reasoning: The Hebrew splice at oshb:Ps.136.13 collates byte (collate.py); the staged source is maqaf-free, so the space inside that quote is the extractor's serialization and the row correctly asserts nothing about maqaf. The span and both seams are right, and stronger than the row says: at the front edge 136:9 opens nominally while 136:10 opens the lamed-participle לְמַכֵּ֣ה (oshb:Ps.136.10), and at the back edge 136:15 opens with a finite verb while 136:16 opens לְמוֹלִ֣יךְ (oshb:Ps.136.16). The row's signal that grammatical form does not itself mark these edges is defensible only in the weak sense that the same head-class change also fires interior to the row at 136:12|13 (לְגֹזֵ֣ר, oshb:Ps.136.13), so form corroborates without uniquely selecting; I do not file that, but the corroboration is available and would carry the row above medium confidence. The rival seam that head-class alone would suggest, 136:12|13, is content-continuous (Egypt through the sea) and 6 verses sits inside the strategy's row-size band, so the span stands. The refrain claim for this span re-derives: all 6 verses carry the plene tail.

challenges.claim: Count-object mismatch: the row writes that the span's verses close with the refrain 'as do all 26 verses of the book' -- 26 is Ps 136's verse count, not the book's, and the refrain is nowhere near a book-wide universal.
challenges.evidence: Ps 136 has 26 verses in both witnesses (verse_map_web.json / verse_map_oshb.json); the book carries 2527 MT / 2461 WEB verses (TOOLKIT.md Phase-0 figures). sweep.py --skel on the refrain tail returns 32 VERSES book-wide for the plene spelling -- Ps 106:1, 107:1, 118:1, 118:2, 118:3, 118:4, 118:29 plus 25 verses of Ps 136 -- and 1 VERSE for the defective spelling (136:3): 33 verses book-wide, 26 of them in this psalm. Naming the swept object first (the refrain tail as a formula, verse unit) yields 'all 26 verses of this psalm', which is what the bytes support.

reviews.reasoning: Both Hebrew splices (oshb:Ps.136.19, oshb:Ps.136.20) collate byte. The span and its seams are sound: 136:16 and 136:17 both open lamed-participle heads, so the row's rejected_alternative is right that no form change divides the wilderness verse from the conquest list, and the 1cp turn at 136:23 is real (שֶׁ֭בְּשִׁפְלֵנוּ זָ֣כַר לָ֑נוּ, oshb:Ps.136.23). The Ps 135 comparison is the interesting part and it does not survive at the tier the row names. Separately noted, not filed as its own item: the strategy reserves typed cross-psalm relations (decision_relations) for the registered pairs -- the doublets, the 9-10 acrostic pair, the 42-43 refrain pair -- while Ps 135|136 is listed only as a hallel block, so calling this notice a typed relation asserts a registry status the inventories do not carry.

challenges.claim: Tier mislabel: the row attributes the Ps 135 comparison to 'byte comparison', but at byte tier the Sihon clause does NOT match -- only the Og clause does -- and the 'two words' difference figure for the land grant is a consonantal figure, not a byte one (4 of 6 words differ at byte tier).
challenges.evidence: Sihon: לְסִיח֤וֹן מֶ֤לֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֗י (oshb:Ps.135.11) against לְ֭סִיחוֹן מֶ֣לֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֑י (oshb:Ps.136.19) -- equal at accent_stripped and skeleton tiers, NOT equal at byte: the accents differ word for word (U+05A4, U+05A4, U+0597 against U+05AD, U+05A3, U+0591 -- verse_map_oshb.json + consonantal_index.json). Og: וּ֭לְעוֹג מֶ֣לֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֑ן (oshb:Ps.135.11) against וּ֭לְעוֹג מֶ֣לֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֑ן (oshb:Ps.136.20) IS byte-identical, so one tier label is covering two different tiers. Land grant: וְנָתַ֣ן אַרְצָ֣ם נַחֲלָ֑ה נַ֝חֲלָ֗ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עַמּֽוֹ (oshb:Ps.135.12) against וְנָתַ֣ן אַרְצָ֣ם לְנַחֲלָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.136.21) plus נַ֭חֲלָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עַבְדּ֑וֹ (oshb:Ps.136.22) differs in exactly 2 of 6 words at skeleton and accent_stripped tiers (positions 3 and 6) but in 4 of 6 words at byte tier (positions 3, 4, 5, 6). Per the campaign's tier discipline the comparison must name the tier it holds at -- consonantal for Sihon and for the two-word figure, byte for Og.

challenges.claim: The cross-psalm comparison is the row's own recorded signal, yet no Ps 135 ref appears in boundary_evidence_refs, and the prose names one Ps 135 'verse' where the comparison in fact spans two.
challenges.evidence: boundary_evidence_refs holds only web:Ps.136.16, web:Ps.136.19, oshb:Ps.136.19, web:Ps.136.20, oshb:Ps.136.20, web:Ps.136.22, web:Ps.136.23 -- nothing from Ps 135 -- so the other side of a claimed byte comparison cannot be checked from the row. The Sihon/Og phrasing sits in oshb:Ps.135.11 (= web:Ps.135.11; Ps 135 is an identity psalm) while the land-grant clause the row compares sits in oshb:Ps.135.12: two verses, not the single 'Ps 135's own Sihon/Og verse' the prose names. Cross-psalm refs are already used in this cluster (web:Ps.33.2, web:Ps.105.1 and the rest in the 136:1-3 row), so nothing bars the mirror here.

reviews.reasoning: Both Hebrew splices (oshb:Ps.136.23, oshb:Ps.136.26) collate byte. The span is right and the front seam is well warranted: 1cp forms enter at 136:23 and 136:24 and are absent from every one of the 19 verses 136:4 through 136:22, so the row's arithmetic checks. The rejected_alternative is sound -- a one-verse coda at 136:26 would break a closing movement that shares the refrain and shows no fresh addressee change. The inclusio evidence, however, is overstated at every tier it is claimed at, and one WEB quotation in this row escapes the mandatory verbatim check.

challenges.claim: The inclusio evidence is mis-tiered and overstated: at byte tier 136:26's opening word does NOT match 136:1's (it matches 136:2's and 136:3's instead), and the stronger rationale form -- that 136:26 repeats 136:1's hodu-le-YHWH opening 'word for word' -- fails at every tier, since the divine-name member changes.
challenges.evidence: הוֹד֣וּ (oshb:Ps.136.1) carries munach U+05A3 after the dalet; ה֭וֹדוּ (oshb:Ps.136.26) carries dehi U+05AD after the he -- not byte-equal; they agree only at accent_stripped and skeleton tiers, and at byte tier 136:26's opening word is identical instead to ה֭וֹדוּ (oshb:Ps.136.2) and to the opening word of oshb:Ps.136.3. The formula itself does not return: 136:1 opens הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה while 136:26 opens ה֭וֹדוּ לְאֵ֣ל -- “Give thanks to Yahweh, for he is good,” (web:Ps.136.1) against “Oh give thanks to the God of heaven,” (web:Ps.136.26). sweep.py --skel on the imperative token returns 15 VERSES book-wide, 4 of them in this psalm (136:1, 136:2, 136:3, 136:26), so the returning word is not proprietary to the 1|26 pair; the defensible claim is a lexical inclusio at skeleton tier over the imperative alone.

challenges.claim: The WEB rendering of 136:26 is quoted in straight quotes, so it bypassed the verbatim check every English quotation is required to pass.
challenges.evidence: check_web_quotes.py on this cluster reports quotes_checked 18, flag_count 0 -- and 18 is exactly the number of CURLY-quoted English quotations across the eight rows; the straight-quoted 'Oh give thanks to the God of heaven,' beside (web:Ps.136.26) is not among them. The content is in fact verbatim against verse_map_web.json, so this is hygiene rather than a misquote, but the rule is curly quotes plus an inline web: ref in the same field for every English quotation, and the checker cannot distinguish a straight-quoted WEB rendering from a straight-quoted gloss.

reviews.reasoning: Ps 137 is an identity psalm (9 verses in both witnesses) and the tiling of its three rows is exact (check_tiling.py over Ps.137.1-Ps.137.9: 9 expected, 9 covered, GREEN). The splice at oshb:Ps.137.1 collates byte and all 4 of its WEB quotations verify verbatim against verse_map_web.json (check_web_quotes.py over the cluster: quotes_checked 18, flag_count 0), including the inner quoted demand at 137:3, which WEB itself sets in quotation marks. The 1cp voice claim re-derives from the Hebrew in all 4 verses of the span -- יָ֭שַׁבְנוּ גַּם בָּכִ֑ינוּ בְּ֝זָכְרֵ֗נוּ (oshb:Ps.137.1), תָּ֝לִ֗ינוּ כִּנֹּרוֹתֵֽינוּ (oshb:Ps.137.2), שְֽׁאֵל֪וּנוּ שׁוֹבֵ֡ינוּ (oshb:Ps.137.3) with its 1cp object, and נָשִׁ֥יר (oshb:Ps.137.4) -- and the narrowing to 1cs at 137:5 (אִֽם אֶשְׁכָּחֵ֥ךְ and תִּשְׁכַּ֥ח יְמִינִֽי) is a genuine tier-1 speaker shift, not a content preference. The selah absence is correct: pmarks_Ps.json holds 71 selah verses book-wide and none in Ps 137, and the row scopes the absence to its span as required. The row quotes across a verse carrying a paseq seg (pmarks_Ps.json paseq: Ps.137.1 = 1, Ps.137.6 = 1, Ps.137.7 = 2, Ps.137.9 = 1), but paseq is seg-layer and absent from the quotable bytes (0 occurrences of U+05C0 in the quoted verses) and the row makes no paseq claim, so no disclosure duty is triggered. One observation, not a defect: check_universals.py raises a WARN on the rejected_alternative's 'no addressee shift between them' as an unswept no-claim; it holds in the psalm's own voice -- no vocative or second-person form stands in 137:1-4 outside the captors' quoted imperative -- but it would read better with the object named.

The splice at oshb:Ps.137.5 collates byte and its 2 WEB quotations verify verbatim. The span is right and both seams are tier-1: 1cs self-imprecation enters at 137:5 against the 1cp of 137:1-4, and 137:7 opens a fresh imperative with a vocative to Yahweh (זְכֹ֤ר יְהוָ֨ה, oshb:Ps.137.7). A two-verse row sits below the strategy's ~4-8 verse band, but that band is explicitly subordinate to tier-1 internal seams and both edges here carry one, so I do not contest the size. The apostrophe claim is slightly loose -- 137:5 has the vocative proper, while in 137:6 the name is a direct object (אֶת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֑ם, oshb:Ps.137.6) and the address is carried by the 2fs suffix of אֶ֫זְכְּרֵ֥כִי -- but the addressee genuinely does not change across the couplet, so that is an observation only. The contrast sentence that closes the rationale is a different matter.

challenges.claim: The rationale describes the whole of 137:7-9 as 'the imprecation against Edom and Babylon that follows in second person address to Yahweh'; address to Yahweh holds only at 137:7, while 137:8-9 address Babylon in 2fs, so the sentence misdescribes two of the three verses it cites.
challenges.evidence: בַּת בָּבֶ֗ל (oshb:Ps.137.8) is a vocative to Babylon, and the second-person forms of that verse are 2fs throughout -- לָ֑ךְ, גְּ֝מוּלֵ֗ךְ, שֶׁגָּמַ֥לְתְּ -- continuing into עֹ֝לָלַ֗יִךְ (oshb:Ps.137.9); WEB reads “Daughter of Babylon, doomed to destruction, he will be happy who repays you, as you have done to us.” (web:Ps.137.8). web:Ps.137.7-Ps.137.9 sits in this row's own boundary_evidence_refs, and the row's rejected_alternative states the position correctly ('137:7 opens a fresh imperative addressed to Yahweh against a third party'), so the rationale sentence is the outlier; the 137:6|7 seam warrant is unaffected.

reviews.reasoning: The splice at oshb:Ps.137.7 collates byte and all 4 of its WEB quotations verify verbatim, including the quoted Edomite cry, which WEB nests inside its own quotation marks at web:Ps.137.7. The voice analysis is accurate on the bytes: 137:7 opens with a 2ms imperative plus the divine-name vocative (זְכֹ֤ר יְהוָ֨ה), the participle הָ֭אֹ֣מְרִים introduces the quoted cry עָ֤רוּ עָ֑רוּ, and the address then turns to Babylon in 2fs and stays there to the psalm's end (בַּת בָּבֶ֗ל, oshb:Ps.137.8; עֹ֝לָלַ֗יִךְ, oshb:Ps.137.9). Grouping the two imprecations as one closing movement is defensible against the rival split at 137:7|8: the addressee does change there, but no first- or third-person report re-enters at the 137:7|8 join, and the row discloses that rival in its rejected_alternative rather than burying it. The selah absence is correct (pmarks_Ps.json holds no selah in Ps 137) and span-scoped as required; the paseq segs at MT 137:7 (2 segs) and 137:9 (1 seg) are seg-layer, unclaimed, and absent from the quotable bytes. High confidence is earned: the span closes the psalm, and its front seam is an imperative-plus-vocative opening -- a tier-1 speech-frame signal, not a content preference.
